title: Notes Java Intro To Object Oriented Programming

items.question: What is Method Overloading in Java?
items.answer: Answer: Method overloading is the process of defining multiple methods with the same name in the same class but with different parameter signatures. The methods can differ in the number, data types, or order of parameters. It is an example of compile-time polymorphism because the compiler selects the appropriate method based on the arguments passed.

items.question: What are the three ways to achieve Method Overloading?
What are the advantages of methods in Java?
items.answer: Answer: Methods provide four important advantages: Readability: Methods make code easier to understand. Modularity or separation of concerns: Each method performs a specific task, keeping the program organized. Code reusability: The same method can be called multiple times without rewriting its logic. Simplified debugging: If a division operation produces an incorrect result, the developer can inspect the division method instead of checking the entire program.

items.question: What is Object Orientation?
items.answer: Answer: The meaning of object orientation can be understood in two ways. In terms of word meaning, object orientation means looking at things from the perspective of objects. In terms of programming, object orientation is a programming paradigm or style of coding intended to solve real-world problems by representing relevant entities as objects and modelling their properties, behaviors, and interactions.

items.question: What are the five basic rules of Object Orientation?
items.answer: Answer: The five basic rules are: The entire world can be viewed as a collection of objects. Every object has a purpose or use in an appropriate context; there is no inherently useless object. Every object belongs to a category, type, or class. Every object interacts with one or more other objects; objects are not always isolated. Every object has properties or attributes and exhibits behaviors or functionalities. These rules help developers identify and understand objects when solving real-world problems.

items.question: What are the properties and behaviors of an Employee object?
items.answer: Answer: An Employee object may have properties such as employee ID and other information required by the application. Its behaviors may include: Attending meetings. Working on tasks or products. Performing assigned responsibilities. Applying for leave. The properties and behaviors depend on the problem being solved and the requirements of the software.

items.question: How can object-oriented thinking be applied to a movie-ticket booking problem?
items.answer: Answer: Consider a customer who wants to watch a movie but must wait in a long queue to purchase a ticket. Even after waiting, the customer may discover that the tickets are sold out. The problem is the inconvenience of purchasing tickets without convenient access to ticket availability and booking facilities. To analyse this problem, the developer must treat the movie-ticket booking scenario as the problem domain and identify the relevant objects. These objects may include: Customer. Movie. Theatre. Show. Show timing. Seat. Ticket. Booking. An online movie-ticket booking service such as BookMyShow provides a real-world example of a system that allows customers to check show information and book available tickets. The example demonstrates how identifying relevant objects helps developers understand the problem before designing the application.

items.question: What are the properties and behaviors of Customer and Seat objects in a ticket-booking system?
items.answer: Answer: Customer object Properties may include: Name. Email ID. Behaviors may include: Booking a ticket. Cancelling a ticket. Seat object Properties may include: Row number. Seat number. Associated theatre or show information. Behaviors may include: Being allocated. Being deallocated. These examples show how objects contain information and participate in the operations of a system. Understanding the properties and behaviors of each object helps developers determine how the booking process should work.

items.question: How can object-oriented thinking be applied to a tea-shop payment problem?
items.answer: Answer: Consider a customer who purchases tea costing ₹5 and pays with a ₹500 note. The shopkeeper does not have enough change to return ₹495. The problem is the inability to complete the payment conveniently because the required change is unavailable. The relevant objects include: The customer who pays the money. The shopkeeper who receives the money. The money involved in the transaction. The example demonstrates why identifying the actual problem and the relevant objects is important. Simply listing objects is not sufficient; the developer must understand how those objects participate in the problem. Once the problem and its relevant objects are understood, their properties, behaviors, and interactions can be analysed to explore a suitable software solution.

items.question: How can the properties, behaviors, categories, and interactions of objects be identified?
items.answer: Answer: An object can be understood by identifying five aspects: Object: The entity being represented. Category or type: The general group to which the object belongs. Properties or attributes: The information that describes the object. Behaviors or functionalities: The actions the object can perform. Interactions: How the object communicates or works with other objects. For example, a student belongs to the Student category. The student can have properties such as name, identification number, age, and marks. Behaviors may include studying, eating, and sleeping. The student interacts with objects such as books, a laptop, and other people. Similarly, a fan can have properties such as brand, color, and number of blades. Its behaviors include rotating and producing airflow.

items.question: How can Object Orientation be used to solve a real-world movie-ticket booking problem?
items.answer: Answer: Consider a customer who wants to watch a popular movie but must wait in a long queue to purchase a ticket. Even after waiting for several hours, the customer may not get a ticket because the available tickets have been sold. The problem is obtaining a movie ticket without wasting time waiting in a queue. To solve this problem, the developer identifies the relevant objects, such as: Customer Movie Theatre Show timing Seat Ticket Booking counter Payment The developer then identifies the properties, behaviors, and interactions of these objects. For example, a customer can book or cancel a ticket, and a seat can be allocated or released. An online booking application such as BookMyShow provides a software-based solution. Customers can check available shows and seats, make payments, and confirm bookings without physically waiting in a queue. The important principle is to identify objects that contribute to solving the actual problem rather than including unrelated objects.

items.question: How can Object Orientation solve the problem of insufficient change at a tea shop?
items.answer: Answer: Suppose a customer purchases tea costing ₹5 but has only a ₹500 note. If the shopkeeper cannot provide ₹495 in change, the payment becomes difficult. The relevant objects are the customer who pays, the shopkeeper who receives the payment, and the money being transferred. A digital payment system can represent the payer, recipient, and payment transaction as interacting entities. The customer can transfer exactly ₹5 without requiring physical change. This example demonstrates how identifying relevant objects and their interactions can help design software that solves a real-world problem.

items.question: What is an Object-Oriented Programming language, and why is Java considered one?
items.answer: Answer: An Object-Oriented Programming (OOP) language supports the object-oriented approach to developing software. Java supports classes, objects, attributes, methods, and interactions between objects. Developers can model real-world entities as classes, create individual objects, and implement their behaviors using methods. For example, a Student class can define student-related properties and methods, while individual student objects represent specific students. Java also supports primitive data types such as int, char, and boolean; therefore, not every value in Java is an object.

items.question: Who is an Object-Oriented thinker, and how does Object Orientation help solve problems?
items.answer: Answer: An object-oriented thinker approaches a problem by viewing its relevant environment as a collection of objects. The person identifies the objects, their categories, properties, behaviors, and interactions and applies the principles of object orientation to model a solution. The process involves identifying the actual problem, treating the relevant scenario as the problem domain, identifying useful objects, understanding their characteristics and interactions, and representing them in software. Once the objects and their interactions are modelled correctly, developers can implement and test a software solution for the original problem.
